simple.meaning: טָהֵר (ṭâhêr) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to be pure (physical sound, clear, unadulterated; Levitically, uncontaminated; morally, innocent or holy).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 95 times across Genesis, Leviticus, Numbers, Joshua, 2 Kings, and 10 more, beginning at Genesis 35:2. Its contexts include offering, blood, priesthood.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to טָהֵר (H2891).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: טָהֵר (ṭâhêr) / H2891 is traced through Genesis 35:2, Leviticus 11:32, Leviticus 12:7, Leviticus 12:8 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.short: to be pure (physical sound, clear, unadulterated; Levitically, uncontaminated; morally, innocent or holy)
definitions.usage: be (make, make self, pronounce) clean, cleanse (self), purge, purify(-ier, self).
